cases.identity_scope: Logical RASDAMAN GDAL driver is distinct from the GDAL-core distribution membership and the archived source-artifact location.

new.namespace: GDAL driver short name retained in archived source
new.kind: driver/function source, not a proven installed replacement

scoped_decisions.claim: Retain the historical RASDAMAN driver ID; OSGeo explicitly relocated that driver source. A repository move alone does not establish a new logical driver.
Record direction core-integrated component → separately archived not-integrated source artifact; do not identify the new artifact as an available stock-GDAL driver or a verified replacement package.

cases.relation_direction: GDAL core RASDAMAN component → OSGeo extra-drivers RASDAMAN source (source relocated; core registration removed in3.7.0)
cases.lineage_evidence: GDAL3.7.0 NEWS names the move; maintainer comment2023-03-12 and receiver commit2023-03-12 agree. Receiver README lists the code as not integrated in the build.

behavior.question: P1
behavior.input_environment: Frozen raster fixture; unchanged RASDAMAN lookup/open in stock GDAL after removal. Driver actually uses a rasql database-query input, so a file-only fixture is not directly applicable. Georeferencing remains a required declared attribute.
behavior.expected: Old call reads required values and georeferencing.
behavior.observed: Static: old registration exists; 3.7.0 registration does not. Receiver driver documentation explicitly lacks georeferencing read/write support. No server/database query or installed before/after pair run.
behavior.status: not demonstrated; unchanged stock-GDAL call predicted unavailable; full georeferencing contract unsupported even before move

behavior.question: P2
behavior.input_environment: Create/CreateCopy with the fixed decoded raster, CRS and nodata; new extra-driver source with an exact compatible GDAL build would be needed.
behavior.expected: Write then old consumer rereads values, CRS and nodata; invalid input rejected.
behavior.observed: Static old driver registration exposes open but no create callback; receiver code is explicitly outside integrated build and docs lack georeferencing.
behavior.status: reject claimed full write-contract compatibility from this evidence; actual executable replacement remains unobserved

cases.counterevidence: Receiver README blanket heading says removed in GDAL3.5, but the same list now includes Rasdaman. Exact move commit/comment and3.7 NEWS contradict applying that heading to this driver. Source continuity also does not prove binary availability.
cases.missing: No before/after executable database input; no compatible extra-driver build; no georeferencing support. No evidence of a mixed historical driver record supplied.
cases.reopen: Pin original driver build and an extra-drivers build compatible with a named GDAL version; provide identical rasql fixture, expected raster and exception cases. A supported write/georeferencing implementation would be required to change P2.
cases.repair: Keep old ID and versioned original citations; add relocation URL and retirement/container status. Keep source-container relationship separate from a drop-in installation claim.
cases.comparison_note: Primary① applies to logical driver identity. If a first decision used distribution artifact as its identity unit, compare the scoped④ decision rather than declaring a disagreement solely from different units.

cases.identity_scope: GDAL ARG driver and its historical format support; no concrete successor supplied.

scoped_decisions.claim: Retain ID and previous version evidence, update deprecated3.8/removed3.9 lifecycle.
Hold: advice to convert to a common format does not nominate a unique successor.

cases.relation_direction: ARG old support → retired in GDAL3.9.0. No successor edge asserted.
cases.lineage_evidence: 3.8 NEWS deprecation and old driver doc name planned3.9 removal;3.9 NEWS and missing registration show execution of that plan.

behavior.question: P1
behavior.input_environment: Same ARG raster, original GDAL call/default environment; frozen raster plus provider ARG fixtures when serializable.
behavior.observed: Provider3.8 tests explicitly set GDAL_ENABLE_DEPRECATED_DRIVER_ARG=YES. After-source registration has no ARG call. No runtime pair was run.
behavior.status: default compatibility not established; after3.9 old driver call predicted unavailable

behavior.question: P2
behavior.input_environment: Create/CreateCopy into a specific replacement format and reread with pinned old consumer.
behavior.observed: Old ARG docs expose Create/CreateCopy/georeferencing. No replacement driver or conversion input/output test supplied.
behavior.status: hold; unspecified alternative is not a tested successor

cases.counterevidence: A passing provider test definition would not establish default-enable support because the test explicitly opts in; a live raster-driver index would not identify ARG as a current driver.
cases.missing: Concrete replacement, identical serialized sample, same-input executions, before-version default config behavior.
cases.reopen: Choose a specified replacement format and old consumer version, convert the same ARG fixture, then compare values/dtype/order/CRS/nodata and malformed-file error behavior.
cases.repair: Retain old URL as versioned historical citation and retired status; do not silently substitute a general driver index or invent a GeoTIFF successor ID.

cases.identity_scope: Named public callable contract within the same SciPy project, including scale direction/default; broad median-absolute-deviation mathematics is not a complete callable identity.

scoped_decisions.claim: Directed replacement with scale-argument adaptation, not unconditional alias.
Split only if an existing record actually mixed the two public callable contracts; no such record was supplied, so no observed split is claimed.

cases.relation_direction: median_absolute_deviation → median_abs_deviation; preserve numeric scale by inverse mapping, not blind name replacement.
cases.lineage_evidence: Maintainer PR11431 introduces new name and divisor semantics; pinned1.5 implementation preserves deprecated old wrapper and inverts numeric scale.

behavior.question: P1
behavior.input_environment: y=[1.,3.,2.], unchanged old public call and defaults,1.4.1→1.5.0.
behavior.expected: Predicted result1.4826, with old multiplicative scale; any new warning handled separately.
behavior.observed: Static1.5 wrapper preserves default1.4826 and forwards reciprocal scale. No runtime pair; warnings-as-errors policy not checked.
behavior.status: qualified static support for old wrapper; complete dtype/NaN/axis/error equivalence unexecuted

behavior.question: P2
behavior.input_environment: Same y with new function under default arguments; also scale=2 distinguishing input.
behavior.expected: Old default1.4826 and old scale=2 result2.0.
behavior.observed: Static new default predicts1.0; new scale=2 predicts0.5. New implementation divides by scale. These are source-derived predictions, not this reviewer’s executions.
behavior.status: reject bare rename/default replacement; adapted replacement can reopen after boundary/dtype/error tests

cases.counterevidence: Same publisher and similar function name do not preserve defaults or argument meaning. Old wrapper preservation gives different P1/P2 answers for the same version pair.
cases.missing: Executed same-input matrix, exact NaN/dtype/error/warning policy for both versions; no actual mixed identity record provided.
cases.reopen: Run pinned1.4.1 and1.5.0 on frozen normal, empty, singleton,2-D, float32, complex and invalid-axis cases; compare old name unchanged and new name with inverse numeric scale separately.
cases.repair: Keep old callable/version citation; link new callable as successor with argument mapping and explicit applicability. Do not overwrite old default semantics.

cases.identity_scope: Each fully-qualified public function/distribution name separately; four pairs in one coordinated naming campaign are not one mathematical function.

scoped_decisions.scope: each old/new fully-qualified name pair in1.6.0
scoped_decisions.claim: Official backwards-compatible names with preserved wrappers/alias declaration. Scope ends at inspected release; later presence not inferred.
Only if an existing record confuses integrate.trapz with stats.trapz; no supplied evidence shows such a mixed record.

cases.relation_direction: Pairwise old name ↔ new alias name in1.6.0; naming recommendation old→new. No equivalence asserted between different pairs.
cases.lineage_evidence: 1.6 NEWS keeps old names; PR12927 and12934 reference issue12924 as one coordinated naming decision. Pinned wrappers forward the same arguments for integration names; stats alias independently declared in release notes.

behavior.question: P1
behavior.input_environment: y=[1.,3.,2.],x=[0.,1.,2.], old integrate names unchanged1.5.4→1.6.0; stats distribution tested only with an appropriate separate provider input.
behavior.observed: Static old/new cumulative and Simpson implementations and1.6 forwarding wrappers read. No provider test execution; stats numerical pair not run.
behavior.status: qualified static compatibility for named wrappers; complete frozen input matrix unexecuted

behavior.question: P2
behavior.input_environment: Same sampled numeric inputs using the corresponding new integrate names, keeping x/dx/axis/initial/even arguments.
behavior.observed: Pinned1.6 wrapper forwarding preserves arguments; identical numerical task is predicted equivalent for that pair. Complete dtype/shape/error and all four-pair behavior not executed.
behavior.status: qualified static support; runtime acceptance remains hold pending required matrix

cases.counterevidence: Short name trapz is ambiguous: integrate is numerical quadrature, stats is a probability distribution. Splitting one pair into unrelated jobs creates duplicate work, but merging different fully-qualified functions discards meaning.
cases.missing: Full executed numerical/exception matrix for each applicable pair; stats implementation pair independently executed; proof beyond1.6.0.
cases.reopen: Execute pinned1.5.4/1.6.0 matrix separately by fully-qualified pair; use distribution-specific inputs for scipy.stats instead of claiming sampled quadrature fixtures cover it.
cases.repair: Add scoped aliases pairwise and preserve original fully-qualified citations. One migration-event count is defensible because both PRs implement the same issue12924 campaign; preserve four target-pair subrows.
